## Rule

Decoded 2026-06-07. The input contract is exactly 4x14 over the full 200k ARC-GEN
corpus (`in_shapes min=max [4,14]`); output is exactly 4x4 (`out_shapes min=max [4,4]`).
Generator source certification: `external/ARC-GEN/tasks/task_cf98881b.py` hardcodes
`colors=(4, 9, 1)` and `size=4`. Columns 4 and 9 are separators. The three active panels are:

- panel 1: rows 0..3, cols 0..3
- panel 2: rows 0..3, cols 5..8
- panel 3: rows 0..3, cols 10..13

For each output cell `(r,c)`, emit the first nonzero color among
`panel1[r,c]`, `panel2[r,c]`, `panel3[r,c]`, scanning left to right. Emit 0 only if all
three are 0. Class-check: LIVE extract is deterministic/clean (`truth --full`
200000/200000; visible 267/267), so byte-equal-vs-LIVE and full truth are both required.

## Algorithm sketch

```python
p1 = grid[:, 0:4]
p2 = grid[:, 5:9]
p3 = grid[:, 10:14]
out = np.where(p1 != 0, p1, np.where(p2 != 0, p2, p3))
```

v6 ONNX uses one custom code vector as both a 1x1 Conv weight and the final channel-ID
comparison vector: `ch0=0, ch1=1, ch4=16, ch9=9, other channels=99`. The three negative-pad
Convs emit panel codes directly from the free one-hot input. `Max(panel1,panel2,panel3)`
implements priority because `16 > 9 > 1 > 0`; `Equal(code, _code)` expands the 4x4 code
canvas to BOOL one-hot; `Pad(BOOL)` writes the free graph output.

## Cost analysis

LIVE cost 8,327 = memory 8,192 + params 135. It slices all three panels as `[1,10,4,4]`
F32 tensors (3 x 640), runs six 1x1 Convs for color/mask extraction, then combines priority
with F32 masks and pads a F32 `[1,10,4,4]` result.

v1 cost 1,047 = memory 888 + params 159. It avoids full one-hot panel slices by using a
3-operand free-input Einsum to create `[1,4,30]` scalar color IDs for rows 0..3, casts to
UINT8, slices the three panels, then uses a BOOL free-output tail.

v2 cost 590 = memory 552 + params 38. It replaces the row-code Einsum with one
negative-pad 1x1 Conv producing `[1,1,4,14]` F32 scalar color IDs directly, then uses UINT8
panel slices and the same tail.

v3 cost 493 = memory 464 + params 29. It emits each panel directly with shared-weight
negative-pad 1x1 Convs:

- `b1_f32`, `b2_f32`, `b3_f32`: 3 x 64 B F32
- `b1`, `b2`, `b3`: 3 x 16 B UINT8 casts
- priority chain: `b1_zero`, `b12`, `b12_zero`, `canvas`: 4 x 16 B
- `onehot4`: 160 B BOOL before final free `Pad(BOOL)->output`
- params: color weight 10 + chids 10 + pads 8 + zero 1 = 29

Final-op families checked per #67/#68: scalar Pad then Equal would materialize a 900-byte
`[1,1,30,30]` canvas, worse than the 160-byte small one-hot + free Pad. A direct Conv output
placer cannot express the priority/equality expansion without dense kernels larger than the
saved memory; the v4 probe confirmed that a final Conv classifier also needs an active-output
geometry mask, otherwise padded cells get a positive ch0 bias.

v6 cost 434 = memory 416 + params 18. Source-backed fixed lane colors allow priority to be
encoded as numeric Max instead of a Where chain:

- `b1_code`, `b2_code`, `b3_code`: 3 x 64 B F32
- `code = Max(...)`: 64 B F32
- `onehot4 = Equal(code, _code)`: 160 B BOOL before final free `Pad(BOOL)->output`
- params: shared `_code` vector 10 + pads 8 = 18

The remaining exact floor appears to be the three 4x4 panel-code reads, one priority reduction,
and the 4x4 one-hot tensor needed before the free full-canvas Pad.

v8 cost 218 = memory 128 + params 90, breaking the stale 434 floor and the 2026-06-21
team-best cost 300. It uses one dilated/cropped Conv to emit two affine features over the
active 4x4 cells:

- `feat`: `[1,2,4,4]` F32 = 128 B
- `w_feat`: `[2,10,1,3]` = 60 params, reading panel columns 0/5/10 with dilation 5
- `w_out`: `[10,2,1,1]` = 20 params
- `bias`: `[10]` = 10 params

The feature embedding is:

```python
f1 = -1 + 4*a - 4*b + 3*c
f2 =      -5*a - 4*b
```

where `a` is panel1 color 4, `b` is panel2 color 9, and `c` is panel3 color 1. The final
Conv is the graph output, padded from 4x4 to 30x30 for free; nonpositive biases keep all
padded cells off. Classifier logits are positive only for the intended channel:

```python
ch0 = -5*f1 + 8*f2
ch1 =  6*f1 + 8*f2 - 4
ch4 =  2*f1 - 2*f2 - 10
ch9 = -8*f1        - 12
```

Rejected beat-300 routes:

- One scalar priority-code Conv + Equal-tail would price at ~272, but no scalar linear code can
  both ignore lower-priority panels when panel1/panel2 fire and still distinguish panel3
  background from panel3 color when earlier panels are empty.
- Grouped Conv can cut dense params, but output channel 9 is forced into the last output group
  and cannot read panel1 channel 4/background for suppression unless `group=1`.
- Three feature planes are straightforward but cost at least 312 (`192 B + 90 + 30`) before
  any shave, so the two-feature rank is the useful threshold.

## Historical Floor Notes

The 2026-06-07/2026-06-12 v6 residual proofs are superseded by v8. Durable lessons kept:
F16 finals add Cast/compare-vector tax; panel fusion via a single off-center Conv needs at least
`[3,10,1,11]` = 330 params; QLinearConv/ConvInteger remain blocked because the graph input is F32
and casting the full `[1,10,30,30]` input costs far more than the saved panel-code bytes.

## Don't-do log

- Do not treat this as an ambiguous filtered-clean task. LIVE truth is 200000/200000, so any
  visible/truth miss is a real bug.
- Do not crop below 4x14 input or 4x4 output. `corpus.build(321, want=200000)` proves
  exactly 4x14 inputs and 4x4 outputs; smaller fixed-window probes would be correctness probes,
  not candidates.
- Do not attempt #137 QLinearConv on this task. QLinearConv requires INT8/UINT8 input; the
  only Conv in v6 runs directly on the F32 graph input. All three U8-input routes are blocked:
  direct QLinearConv(F32) fails checker; Cast(F32→U8) = 9,000 B intermediate; named-input
  bridge charges the original F32 graph tensor (36,000 B — scorer renames "input"→"safe_name_0").
  Same root cause killed task192 v13/v14. #137 only applies when there is a previously
  quantized U8 intermediate to feed into a downstream Conv.
- Do not rebuild from three `[1,10,4,4]` one-hot panel slices unless using it as a clarity
  fallback; the scalar color-ID panel route is much cheaper.
- Do not replace the priority `Where` chain with `Max`/OR/Bitwise assembly. Cells can contain
  multiple nonzero panel colors, and the required color is the leftmost nonzero, not the raw
  max or union. The v5/v6 Max route is valid only because it uses source-backed priority codes
  `16 > 9 > 1`, not the raw color IDs.
- Do not move the final `Equal` after a scalar 30x30 Pad. That makes a charged 900-byte scalar
  canvas; the staged v3 small one-hot + free BOOL Pad is cheaper.
- Do not use the v4 final Conv-as-output classifier without an active 4x4 geometry feature.
  It scores 434 locally but visible-gates 0/267 because Conv bias makes ch0 positive in padded
  cells outside the output shape.
